deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for service=rl-inferaptor region=eu-west-1 rollout_id=cr-2001 :rocket:
maria: noticing the rollback automation didn't trigger when health checks spiked. traffic stayed split 70/30 to canary for ~3m, then error budget burned. :eyes:
jonathan: looking at gitops controller logs — splitter webhook returned 504 and the state machine stalled waiting for confirmation.
maria: snippet from controller log:
```
2026-03-19T08:12:23Z ERROR splitter: webhook call failed: context deadline exceeded (timeout 15s)
2026-03-19T08:12:27Z WARN  splitter: desired state not observed, waiting
```
ashley: can you paste the canary probe config? my hunch is readiness/liveness mismatch causing transient failures that the automation treats as non-fatal.
maria: canary config excerpt:
```
canary:
  target: 0.3
  min_consecutive_failures: 2
  healthcheck:
    path: /healthz
    success_threshold: 3
    failure_threshold: 1
    period_seconds: 5
```
ashley: ah — success_threshold=3 with period 5s means it needs 15s of success to flip. webhook TTL is 15s too. if webhook retries are limited, a transient 1-2s spike kills the confirmation window.
sre-oncall: also saw spot GPU fallback in the same window — autoscaler pulled new nodes but they were slow to register (capacity pressure). combines poorly with small success window.
jonathan: immediate mitigation: increase webhook timeouts and retries in gitops-controller, and reduce success_threshold to 2 for this service (safer flip). long term: make splitter confirmation idempotent (poll observed state instead of single webhook ack).
maria: manual workaround executed:
`kubectl annotate traffic-splitter/rl-inferaptor canary.forceFlip=true --overwrite`
then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/rl-inferaptor-canary` — traffic split corrected and rollback triggered.
ashley: created PR to bump controller retries + extend webhook TTL to 30s, and to add a circuit-breaker for concurrent webhook failures. tagging infra for patch review: @jonathan @sre-oncall :+1:
jonathan: agree. also add a telemetry metric to correlate webhook latencies with node registration times and GPU pool scaling events — helps debug future cost/latency tradeoffs.
maria: noted. will follow up with a postmortem (short) describing the sequence: probe window mismatch + webhook timeout + slow spot GPU registration -> delayed rollback -> brief SLO breach.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout cr-2001 marked status=rolled-back by manual action (maria) at 2026-03-19T08:14:59Z :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks everyone. plan: patch controller TTL, lower success_threshold for aggressive canaries, add poll fallback. I'll post remediation PRs shortly. :wave:
